tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy cold-season single-column run, data/eqwefic/noahcold_scm, dumped by ctessum-claude/WRF branch earthsciml-instrumented-noahcold and replayed through the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) kernels/noah_driver at ESM_DT = 1e-6 s. Inputs are the dumped SFLX arguments (real32 values widened). SNFRAC and ALCALC are called early in SFLX, before the NOPAC/SNOPAC branch -- but NOT before the new snowfall is added to the pack, so on a snowing step the cover SFLX diagnoses is that of the pack INCLUDING this step's accumulation and is therefore dt-dependent after all. Measured over the 67 pack steps, sncovr moves by up to 2.4e-5 and the albedo by 5.8e-6 between ESM_DT = 0.01 s and 1e-6 s, so the reference here is taken at 1e-6 s, where it is the input-state limit this component computes. A residual of that increment survives even there on the thinnest packs -- case A's 5e-6 m pack moves sncovr by 2.4e-9 relative over a 1e-6 s step -- which is what sets the 1e-8 bound below; it bounds the REFERENCE, not the component. A second dt dependence is easier to miss still: ALCALC advances the snow-age accumulator snotime1 BEFORE it uses it, so the age that sets the albedo is the POST-update one. This component takes that post-update age as its `snotime1` parameter and the test supplies the replay's snotime1_out, which makes the albedo exact rather than dt-sensitive. sndens is referenced against the density SNOPAC leaves at the END of the step, which at this step size is the input-state ratio to well within the bound below. NOTE which background albedo and emissivity are the right ones: the dump's `albbrd` and `embrd` are the values the DRIVER carried in, and REDPRM overwrites both by greenness before SFLX uses them, so the test supplies the greenness-selected values (albedomin and emissmax on this shdfac >= shdmax column) -- exactly what soil_veg_parameters.esm computes. Using the dumped `embrd` instead moves the emissivity by 7 %. Replay floors from the cold-season notes bound what can honestly be claimed: sncovr 2.2e-5, albedo 9.8e-8. Step 101 of case A, snow accumulating onto initially bare frozen ground (partial cover throughout); the pack is on the sub-freezing SNOPAC branch.
